title: Guiro (notched gourd)
summary: The guiro is a hollow gourd cut with parallel notches and scraped with a stick, making a rasping, rattling sound. A long stroke runs the whole length of the notches, a short scratch lives in the middle, and a knock on the end gives a dry wooden beat.
howToPlay: Four places are lit: Down and Up along the notches, Scratch in the middle, Knock at the rounded end.
The stick travels along the gourd as each stroke sounds; the notches it crosses gleam.
A ring closes on the place to strike. Keep the long strokes smooth and the knock crisp.
rules: A stroke on the beat is perfect, a near one is good, and extra strokes cost points.
The round ends when the last stroke has been judged; the score is the share of the best possible.
heritageNote: In Caribbean dance music the guiro rasps through the rhythm section, a long scrape on the beat and quick scratches that fill the gaps.
